claims.text: CFRP consists of a thermosetting or thermoplastic polymer matrix containing dispersed carbon fibers.
CFRP enables lighter designs than conventional metals.
CFRP provides superior overall performance compared with conventional metals.
CFRP has a high strength-to-weight ratio.
CFRP has excellent fatigue resistance.
Optimizing fiber orientation during fabrication improves the fiber alignment of CFRP.
Optimizing interface bonding during fabrication improves the quality of the fiber-matrix interface.
Aligned carbon fibers provide high stiffness and strength.
The polymer matrix has sufficiently low density to reduce composite weight.
Combining aligned carbon fibers with a low-density polymer matrix reduces weight while maintaining or improving mechanical performance.
The proposed composite architecture maintains or improves fatigue resistance.
The proposed composite architecture maintains or improves impact resistance.
CFRP samples will match or exceed the tensile strength of comparable aluminum-alloy samples.
CFRP samples will match or exceed the stiffness of comparable aluminum-alloy samples.
CFRP samples will match or exceed the fatigue limits of comparable aluminum-alloy samples.
Conventional aluminum alloys generally have greater weight than CFRP components used in similar applications.
Conventional aluminum alloys generally have lower fatigue performance than CFRP.
CFRP performance benefits are most pronounced in weight-critical aerospace and automotive applications.
Environmental extremes, especially high temperatures, can compromise polymer properties and reduce CFRP performance.
CFRP is predicted to achieve at least a 20% weight reduction while matching or exceeding aluminum in tensile strength, stiffness, and fatigue life under identical tests.
